subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` as a core config surface now, and what should happen to no-override `bootstrap-extra-files` extras in subagent and cron sessions?
rationale: The source gap and user demand are real, but the PR changes prompt context, session-state behavior, public config, and documented hook semantics in ways automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Require compatibility before merge
options.body: Keep no-override hook-loaded `AGENTS.md`/`TOOLS.md` behavior intact, make stricter hook exclusion apply only to explicit tiers, and document the new config contract before landing.

options.title: Accept stricter no-override semantics
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally require `bootstrapTier: "full"` for hook extras in lean sessions, but the PR should then include public docs, upgrade notes, and tests that name the behavior change.

options.title: Pause or replace the config knob
options.body: Defer this PR behind broader bootstrap/context-selection design if maintainers prefer existing `contextInjection`, bootstrap budgets, or a different selector contract.

recommendation.title: Require compatibility before merge
recommendation.body: Keep no-override hook-loaded `AGENTS.md`/`TOOLS.md` behavior intact, make stricter hook exclusion apply only to explicit tiers, and document the new config contract before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined signal from subagent bootstrap history and prior review routing on the linked issue.
